system.name: ViVerBench
system.one_liner: A benchmark of 16 visual-verification tasks in 6 categories that tests whether multimodal LLMs can judge if a visual outcome is correct during reasoning and generation.

content.variant_note: six grey category panels holding 16 uniform task cards, each with prompt, answer, explanation and a thumbnail
content.argues: Visual verification covers many kinds of checks, from concept existence and spatial relations to game states and formulas, and each is hard enough that even false samples need careful explanation.
content.subject: Sixteen false-labelled benchmark samples, one per sub-task, grouped under six categories.

elements.name: Concept Existence
elements.role: category of tasks that check whether a described concept is present in an image
elements.drawn_as: grey rounded panel with a centred bold banner, holding the cards Object, Attribute, Abstract Patterns

elements.name: Object Relationship
elements.drawn_as: grey panel with banner, holding Spatial and Non-Spatial

elements.name: Image Annotation
elements.role: category checking boxes, pointers and counts drawn on images
elements.drawn_as: grey panel with banner, holding Bounding Box, Pointing, Counting

elements.name: World Dynamics
elements.role: category checking physical plausibility of images and sequences
elements.drawn_as: grey panel with banner, holding Static Physics and Dynamic Physics

elements.name: State Value Evaluation
elements.role: category judging whether a state or move in a game, robot or interface moves toward the goal
elements.drawn_as: grey panel with banner, holding Maze, FrozenLake, Robotics, GUI

elements.name: STEM
elements.role: category checking charts and formulas against code or text
elements.drawn_as: grey panel with banner, holding Charts and LaTeX

elements.name: task cards (16)
elements.role: one false sample per sub-task: Object, Attribute, Abstract Patterns, Spatial, Non-Spatial, Bounding Box, Pointing, Counting, Static Physics, Dynamic Physics, Maze, FrozenLake, Robotics, GUI, Charts, LaTeX
elements.drawn_as: rounded white card with 1.25 pt grey outline, grey tab title at the upper left, text at left and a thumbnail at right

elements.name: Prompt
elements.role: the task statement or the description the image must satisfy, shortened with ellipses
elements.drawn_as: bold label followed by 2-4 lines of 6 pt serif text

elements.name: Answer: False
elements.drawn_as: one line, bold label and the word False

elements.name: Explanation
elements.drawn_as: bold label followed by 2-3 lines of text

elements.name: red key phrases
elements.role: the part of the prompt the image gets wrong, such as 'bearing a red flag', 'a white flower pot', 'solid black diamond', "color='red',"
elements.drawn_as: dark red text spans inside the Prompt lines

relations.what: the text describes the image beside it
the red phrase is what the Explanation says the image fails to show

two narrow screenshots side by side at the card's right

examples.what: sixteen false-labelled verification samples, one per sub-task, each with a shortened prompt, Answer: False and an explanation
examples.form: uniform cards with Prompt, Answer and Explanation lines and a thumbnail; ellipses mark cut text

idioms.drawn_as: task card with a tab title, prompt, ground-truth answer and explanation beside the sample image; no model answers or ticks

content.reading_order: Starts at the Concept Existence banner top left and runs down the left column, then the right column from World Dynamics to STEM; inside a card the eye goes tab, Prompt with its red phrase, Explanation, then the thumbnail.

layout.arrangement_note: Two columns of grey rounded category panels with centred banner titles; each panel stacks two to four uniform cards with a grey tab title, three text lines on the left and one thumbnail on the right.

palette.used_for: sub-task title tabs of the 16 cards
light grey ground of the six category panels (at 0.75 opacity)

style.stroke: 1.25 pt mid-grey outline on the 16 cards; no other strokes
style.font: serif (TeX Gyre Pagella, Palatino-like) 6 pt body with bold field labels, 8.5 pt bold tab titles, 10 pt bold banners

encoding.color_means: grey = structure (banner, tab, panel); red text = the phrase that makes the sample false; all other colour comes from the thumbnails
encoding.line_style_means: one solid grey outline = card boundary
encoding.shape_means: wide centred banner = category; small tab at the upper left of a card = sub-task; rounded card = one sample
encoding.marker_means: Answer: False is the ground-truth label; ellipses mark text cut from the prompt
encoding.emphasis: Red phrases in the prompts point to what is wrong; large bold banners make the six categories the first thing read.
reusable_patterns: grey category panels with centred banners holding titled cards
one card template repeated: tab title, Prompt, Answer, Explanation, right-aligned thumbnail
red spans in the prompt that point to the error
only failing samples shown to dramatise difficulty
weaknesses: about 4,000 characters in 6 pt type are hard to read in print
thumbnails are about 40 x 40 pt, so the visual evidence of the error is hard to see

own: 16 samples from the benchmark with their prompts, answers, explanations and images (several images are model-generated data under test)
drawn: grey panels, banners, tabs and card outlines

objects: thumbnails of scenes, maze, FrozenLake, robot, GUI, chart and formula

lessons.what_to_learn: Show a benchmark's scope as grey category panels that each hold uniform cards (tab title, Prompt, Answer, Explanation, thumbnail) and colour the offending phrase red so each failure reads at a glance.
lessons.suits: Benchmarks with many sub-tasks across several categories that need one real sample each; example galleries where every card carries the same fields.

sections: 3 ViVerBench: Assessment of MLLMs on Visual Verification (p.3)
evidence: ViVerBench Overview. We show only the false data samples to better highlight data difficulty.
It comprises 16 tasks across 6 main categories
Each data sample is labeled with a true/false answer, and the two categories are evenly distributed in the benchmark.

summary: The paper introduces a generative universal verifier and ViVerBench, a benchmark for judging whether visual outcomes produced during reasoning and generation are correct. Figure 1 is the benchmark overview. Six grey category panels in two columns (Concept Existence, Object Relationship, Image Annotation; World Dynamics, State Value Evaluation, STEM) hold 16 rounded task cards, one per sub-task such as Object, Maze, FrozenLake, GUI, Charts or LaTeX. Every card follows one template: a tab title, Prompt, Answer: False and Explanation lines with the key phrase in red, and a small thumbnail (generated scene, game state, screenshot, chart, formula). Only false samples are shown to stress difficulty. The look is flat grey, Palatino-style serif, with dense small text.
summary_zh: ViVerBench是评测视觉验证能力的基准。图1用六个灰色类别面板（概念存在、物体关系、图像标注、世界动态、状态价值评估、STEM）收纳16张子任务卡片，每张含提示、答案False、解释（关键词标红）和缩略图，只展示错误样本以突出难度。
notes: The digest labels TeXGyrePagella as sans; it is a Palatino-like serif in the preview. Several thumbnails (castle, cottage, bookshelf, street artist, cartoon faces) look model-generated, but they are benchmark samples, so they are listed as own data. The caption is cut off in the preview.
